messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a weird credit routing on last invoice. Promo credits from the Q4 partner bundle were consumed against payg usage instead of our Reserved GPU commitment lines. Can someone check if region tags caused this?

sam: Yikes. Which invoice # / timeframe?

maya: Invoice 2026-02-28 (lines around GPU-reserve-us-west-2). Thread start ts 1765123456. I pulled billing CSV, looks like credits labeled EU_PARTNER_PROMO ended up hitting `us-west-2:payg-gpu` rather than `us-west-2:reserved-commit`.

jules: tagging infra — we had a networking provisioning failure in us-west earlier that forced failover to shared pools for ~18h on Feb 25. Could be the reason reserved capacity wasn't used, so credits flowed to payg.

arthur: billing note: credits apply to the invoice line item that was actually billed. If reserved instances didn't produce usage there was nothing to offset, so credits fallthrough to other lines. We can request a manual reallocation but need strong justification and support ticket to the cloud provider.

maya: Understood. We need a paper trail showing the reserved pool was unavailable due to our outage so provider will accept retroactive correction. Jules — can you supply the incident id + capacity usage graph?

jules: Yep. Incident ID INC-2026-02-25-usw-provision. I have a grafana snapshot and the autoscaler logs showing failed attachments between 03:12 and 21:27 UTC. Pasting snippet: ```error: attach_gpus failed: network timeout to hypervisor 10.2.45.8; retries exhausted```

eli: Also worth noting: some nodes were created in a different AZ (us-west-2b vs us-west-2a) because of a placement fallback. Reserved commit tags are AZ-scoped in the billing system, so if VM usage landed in 2b but commit is for 2a, credits won't match.

karen: From account side, customer credits (the partner promo) are only allowed to apply to usage within the same geography per contract clause 4.2. If some usage fell into different AZs the cloud provider might still treat it as same region, but we should verify.

sam: Action items: 1) Jules to attach incident artifacts and az placement logs. 2) Eli to produce a short usage mapping: reserved-commit-line -> actual usage by AZ/time window. 3) Arthur to open a billing support case with cloud provider and request reallocation / retro credit citing outage. 4) Finance to hold any further automated reconciliations until we know outcome.

maya: Adding target: need this fixed before month-end close (Mar 5). If cloud vendor declines, we need a Redwood-side journal entry to move promo credit from payg to reserved commit line for internal accounting reconciliation.

arthur: I'll file the support case now. Support ticket number will be posted here once created. We should include the following payload in the ticket: 
```
- Invoice: 2026-02-28
- Promo credit IDs: PROMO-PLAT-Q4-2025 (x1)
- Affected lines: us-west-2 payg GPU (line ids: L-55321,L-55322)
- Evidence: INC-2026-02-25-usw-provision, grafana snapshot, autoscaler logs, AZ placement report
```

ops-bot: Billing alert: invoice 2026-02-28 had credits applied to payg lines totaling $42,600.709.

eli: Quick note — to strengthen the case include the scheduler debug trace that shows allocation attempted against reserved pool: `scheduler.assign(reserved_pool_usw, vm_id=... ) -> attach_gpus() -> timeout`. That proves we intended to use reserved capacity.

jules: Uploaded artifacts to /shared/incidents/INC-2026-02-25-usw-provision (grafana, logs, scheduler traces, az-placement.csv). Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-02-25-usw-provision

sam: Thanks. Arthur, once you get the cloud support case number, ping me and I'll prepare the GL reclassification template in case we need to do the journal entry.

arthur: Case created: CLOUD-9876123. Submitted evidence bundle. Support ETA 3 business days.

maya: If cloud vendor denies reallocation, proposal B: we absorb a one-time internal credit transfer from the partner promo pool to reserved commit accounting and then invoice the partner for a make-good if contract allows. Need legal + partnerships signoff.

karen: I can loop in partnerships/legal once we have final ruling. FYI partner contract clause suggests a remedy but not automatic.

eli: Also flagging optimization idea: if reserved pools are AZ-scoped and fragile to placement fallback, we should introduce a tag-agnostic reserved buffer that can accept overflow during incidents — reduces chance of payg bleeding in outage windows. Ops backlog item.

jules: Agreed. Will create an RFC for a soft-reserve overlay (low-cost, short-lived) to catch attach failures.

sam: For the immediate billing window: Finance will mark the $42.6k as disputed until resolution. Please avoid moving those credits in the accounting system until we have cloud response.

maya: Thanks all — keeping this channel for status. I'll update if partner asks for an interim explanation. :thumbsup:
